title: Contract Clause Extraction and Risk Flags
summary: Extract key clauses, dates and obligations from executed and incoming contracts, compare them with your playbook and flag deviations, with every item linked to the clause it came from.

seo.title: Contract Clause Extraction and Risk Flags | VipraTech
seo.description: AI that extracts clauses, renewal dates and obligations from contracts, compares them with your playbook and flags risks for lawyer review.

problem.intro: Most organisations hold years of executed contracts as scanned PDFs on shared drives: MSAs, SOWs, leases, distribution and vendor agreements, each with amendments and side letters. Nobody can say quickly which contracts auto-renew next quarter, which carry uncapped indemnities or which need consent on a change of control.

pain_points.title: Unknown obligations
pain_points.detail: Renewal dates, notice periods, exclusivity and minimum commitments are buried in clauses that nobody re-reads after signing.

pain_points.title: Amendments change the picture
pain_points.detail: Addenda and side letters modify the main agreement, and a review that misses them gives the wrong answer.

pain_points.title: Inconsistent first-pass review
pain_points.detail: Different lawyers flag different risks in incoming paper, so the business gets uneven turnaround and advice.

pain_points.title: Scanned and stamped documents
pain_points.detail: Contracts executed on stamp paper, signed by hand and scanned at low quality defeat simple text search.

solution.overview: We build a contract review pipeline that reads executed and incoming contracts, including scanned and stamped copies, splits them into clauses and links amendments to the clauses they change. It extracts the terms your team cares about, such as parties, term, renewal, termination rights, notice periods, liability caps, indemnities, governing law, dispute resolution, assignment, change of control and data protection, each with a citation to clause and page. Extracted positions are compared with your playbook and fallbacks, and deviations are flagged with the reason. Lawyers review flags on one screen, and confirmed data feeds your contract repository and renewal calendar.
capabilities: Clause segmentation for scanned, stamped and signed contracts in English and Hindi
Links amendments, addenda and side letters to the clauses they modify
Extracts parties, dates, renewal, termination, liability, indemnity, governing law and dispute resolution
Compares each position with your standard and fallback positions
Flags missing clauses, such as data protection or limitation of liability
Builds an obligation and renewal calendar from confirmed data

workflow.title: Collect contracts
workflow.detail: Contracts are loaded from shared drives, the CLM or email, and grouped with their amendments.

workflow.title: Segment and read
workflow.detail: OCR and layout analysis split each document into numbered clauses and schedules.

workflow.title: Extract key terms
workflow.detail: Agreed fields are extracted, each with a confidence score and a clause citation.

workflow.title: Compare with the playbook
workflow.detail: Positions are checked against your standard and fallback positions, and gaps are flagged.

workflow.title: Lawyer review
workflow.detail: A lawyer confirms, corrects or dismisses each flag and each low-confidence field.

workflow.title: Update the repository
workflow.detail: Confirmed terms go to the contract repository, and renewal and notice alerts are scheduled.

inputs: Executed contracts, including scanned and stamped copies
Your contract playbook and fallback positions
List of fields and risk categories to track
outputs: Clause register with citations to clause and page
Deviation and missing-clause flags with reasons
Portfolio view of risk positions across contracts
human_in_the_loop: A lawyer confirms every flagged deviation and every low-confidence field before it enters the register. Risk ratings are suggestions; legal decides what is acceptable and what to renegotiate.
integrations: Document management system such as iManage or SharePoint
Calendar and task tools for renewal alerts
ERP or procurement system for vendor master data
guardrails: Every extracted value cites the clause and page it came from
Playbook positions owned and versioned by the legal team
No contract marked acceptable without lawyer review
Documents processed in your environment, and models do not train on them
Matter or business-unit access controls carried into the tool
compliance_notes: Contracts contain personal data of signatories and counterparties; designed to support DPDP Act 2023 security safeguards and access control.
The tool supports lawyers' review; it does not provide legal advice.

faqs.q: Will it work on old scanned contracts?
faqs.a: Yes, within limits. OCR handles most scans and stamp-paper first pages, and fields it cannot read confidently go to a lawyer. The pilot report separates accuracy for digital and scanned documents.

faqs.q: Can we use our own playbook?
faqs.a: Yes. The playbook is configuration owned by your legal team, with standard positions, fallbacks and escalation rules for each clause.
It links amendments and side letters to the clauses they change and shows the current position with its history. Lawyers confirm the link when it is uncertain.

faqs.q: Is our data used to train models?
faqs.a: No. We use models and settings that do not retain or train on your documents, and processing stays in your cloud account or chosen region.
